subject: puma
title: Pumas Are Loners. Near a Penguin Beach, They Met 254 Times

scenes.text: Pumas avoid each other. On one beach, they keep meeting.
In Patagonia, pumas returned to a park where over forty thousand pairs of penguins nest.
On land, penguins are almost defenseless. The cats started hunting them.
Penguin-hunting pumas met each other two hundred fifty-four times. Pumas that skipped penguins? Four.
With that much food, there's nothing to fight over.
The park now holds over twice as many pumas as anywhere ever measured. Loners, sharing a beach.

description:
Pumas are usually solitary, but at Monte Leon National Park in Argentina, cats that hunt Magellanic penguins keep running into each other.
Of 14 GPS-collared pumas, the penguin eaters recorded 254 encounters with each other, mostly within a kilometre of a colony of over 40,000 breeding pairs; pumas that ignored penguins met just four times. Puma density there is more than double the highest ever recorded.
Why do you think the cats stopped fighting?
first_comment: Pumas were wiped out here about a century ago and only came back after ranching stopped. Should the park protect the cats or the penguins?
